Subject: MAP & billing framework for Acme evaluation -> production

Jordan —

Great speaking earlier. As discussed, I attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (Acme_MAP_v1.2.pdf) that maps the evaluation milestones to commercial triggers so procurement and your engineering leads can align on timing. High level: 

- Evaluation (30 days): PoC access, technical checkpoints (weeks 1 & 3). No billed usage during evaluation beyond small setup charge (see note).
- Ramp (0–3 months post-eval): Pilot pricing applies once we transition to dedicated capacity; customer commit required to access ramp discounts.
- Production (3–12 months): Committed units with tiered discounts based on annualized commit.

Commercial items to confirm for our mutual action plan:
1) Pricing & discounts: evaluation discount provided as credits for first 30 days; ramp discounts keyed to a minimum commit (we typically recommend a $150k ARR baseline for the first discount tier).
2) Billing start date: typically we invoice from the first month after go-live OR first full month after receipt of PO — whichever you prefer; we can align to your procurement constraints.
3) Payment terms: standard Net30; Net60 can be approved for enterprise accounts with an executed contract and valid PO on file.
4) Invoicing cadence: monthly, in arrears. We can issue a single consolidated invoice for committed capacity or split invoices (setup, reserved capacity, overage) — let me know preference.
5) PO requirements: If Acme requires a PO before invoicing, we need PO number and billing contact ahead of the billing start date.

Action items I propose:
- Acme confirms procurement contact and PO lead (name/email).
- Acme confirms whether Net60 is required and whether billing should wait until PO receipt or be tied to go-live.
- Redwood to version and lock the MAP once procurement confirms timelines.

I copied Marissa (Finance) to fast-track the Net60/PO question. If you want, I can convert the MAP into a short mutual checklist for procurement to sign to speed approval.

Attachments: Acme_MAP_v1.2.pdf (MAP draft)

Thanks —
Laura Bennett

Laura —

Finance reviewed Acme's request. Summary and recommended approach: 

1) Net60 approval: Finance will approve Net60 for enterprise accounts provided: 
   - Fully executed Master Services Agreement (MSA) or equivalent purchase schedule on file, and
   - Valid PO is received before the first invoice.

2) Billing start date (approved options): 
   Option A (preferred for revenue clarity): Billing begins on the first calendar month following the PO receipt date (e.g., PO received 9/10 -> billing starts 10/01).
   Option B (if customer needs billing tied to go-live): Billing begins the first full month after go-live; PO must still be provided within 30 days of go-live.

3) Invoicing cadence: Monthly, in arrears. Invoices will include a line for reserved capacity and separate lines for overages and one-time setup.

4) Documentation & PO requirements: PO must reference Redwood's legal entity (Redwood Inference, Inc.), include deal id ACME-2026-Q3-01, and specify billing address and remittance instructions. We will provide a one-page PO template for procurement to fill (happy to attach).

5) Discount guardrails: Discounts tied to commit will be captured in the SOW (e.g., "Ramp Discount: X% applied once Acme confirms an annualized commit of $150,000 within 30 days of go-live"). Finance needs that language in either the SOW or the PO.

I attached Sample_Invoice_Schedule.pdf and will send the PO template to procurement@acme.com once we have the procurement contact.

If this works, we can have Laura send a short confirmation to Jordan and procurement and request the PO by Sep 7 to keep the onboarding timeline.

Thanks —
